title: What the Stream Wrote: Byte Order, a Float That Took Eight Bytes, and a String That Is Not the Bytes You Meant

questions.question: A Qt program streams the 16 bit number 0x0102 with a default QDataStream to a device whose data sheet says least significant byte first. What does the device see?
How many bytes does stream << 1.5f write by default, and with single precision?
What does stream << QString("ab") write?
options: A four byte length in bytes and then UTF-16
questions.explanation: 00 00 00 04 00 61 00 62. The format of the lesson writes the length byte and the UTF-8 itself.

questions.question: The lesson's frame for id 258, value 1.5 and the name micro-s is how many bytes?
A QDataStream runs out of bytes in the middle of a read. What happens?
options: It sets the status to ReadPastEnd and the value read is set to zero
questions.explanation: Code that never asks for the status sees zeros. The second 16 bit number was 0, not the 88 it held before.

questions.question: Which three questions does decode_reading ask?
options: Is it short, is it long, is it valid
Is the id zero, is the value zero, is the name empty
Is it big endian, is it a float, is it UTF-16
Did the fixed part read without error, were all the name bytes read, and is the stream at its end
questions.explanation: All 14 prefixes of the frame, one byte too many and a length byte of 200 were refused.
